profile.headline: Chief Technology Officer at Hooky AI, Inc.
profile.summary:
25+ years of software development and infrastructure experience. From building and racking servers and configuring network and telephony equipment to designing container platforms and distributed systems. Worked with Docker and Kubernetes since their earliest releases and contributed to Kubernetes, Docker, and multiple CNCF projects in Go and Rust. Longtime interest in security and system internals, from hardware and embedded devices to operating systems. Passionate about continuous learning, educating developers, and growing communities.

•   Languages: Go, Ruby (Rails), PHP, SQL, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Bash; familiar with Rust, Java, C#, Python.
•   Containers, runtimes, and orchestration: Kubernetes, Docker, Podman, runc, service meshes, service discovery.
•   Security: Offensive security, prompt injection and XPIA, incident response, application security, HSMs and secure enclaves.
•   Databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, DB2, Cassandra, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka.
•   Distributed systems: High availability, scalability.
•   Media: Video encoding, HLS, MPEG-DASH, MPEG-TS, RTMP, GStreamer, FFmpeg.
•   Interests: Information security, Linux internals, containers and container orchestration, developer tooling, embedded devices.

Open Source:
•   SkyDNS: Wrote SkyDNS, which kube-dns used for DNS-based service discovery in Kubernetes until CoreDNS replaced it in 1.11.
•   Upstream contributions: Kubernetes, Docker, Go, go-mysql, rust-media-libs, metric_fu, asset_packager, and other open-source projects.
•   Ruby on Rails: Implemented unobtrusive JavaScript support for Rails 3.0, wrote its initial jQuery and Prototype drivers, and contributed significantly to making it JavaScript-framework agnostic.
•   rtmp-switcher: Built a proof-of-concept live video switcher and compositor in Rust and GStreamer
•   Original author of Virtual Kubelet (a CNCF project), which lets Kubernetes schedule pods onto external providers such as serverless platforms.
•   Contributed to Krustlet (a CNCF project), for running WebAssembly workloads on Kubernetes.

Other Accolades:
•   Co-author Go in Action
•   Delivered closing keynote at KubeCon 2016
•   Technical Reviewer for several books by O'Reilly, Manning, and Pragmatic Programmers

Community:
•   Organizer GopherCon - Annual Go conference
•   Founded the Go Tampa and Cloud Native Tampa meetups.
•   Founder and co-host of Go Time, a Go podcast.

Specialties: Go, Ruby, Rails, Javascript,  High Scale, High Availability, Kubernetes, Docker, Multimedia

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
•   Focused on AI security as part of a working group.
•   Developing processes for AI-based vulnerability scanning and threat modeling AI-enabled systems.
•   Delivered indirect prompt injection (XPIA) training and demos across Azure Core.
•   Created a cloud cost reduction strategy that has saved over $200K in its early stages.
•   Helped train engineers on containers and Kubernetes.
•   Helped define the organization's Principal IC role and expectations.
•   Ran discovery and built proofs of concept for platform projects, including link detonation and domain threat intelligence, AI eval and coding harnesses.
•  Managed security incident response and drove content governance.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineering Manager
positions.description:
•   Led the Learn Video team, owning live (Learn TV) and on-demand video for Learn and other Microsoft properties, from encoding, captioning, and translation to hosting and serving.
•   Led development of Auteur, an open-source Rust and GStreamer service for scheduling and compositing live video feeds, replacing the rtmp-switcher proof of concept.
•   Led the Learn UX team, which owned the shared UX components and design system for all of Microsoft Learn.
•   Led the authoring tools and editor teams, owning Learn's web-based editor and VS Code extensions.

positions.title: Principal Cloud Advocate
positions.description:
•   Original author of Virtual Kubelet (now a CNCF sandbox project), which lets Kubernetes schedule pods onto external providers such as serverless container platforms.
•   Contributed to Krustlet (a CNCF sandbox project), a Rust kubelet for running WebAssembly workloads on Kubernetes, and presented it at the live@Manning Kubernetes Conference in 2020.
•   Focused on Linux, containers, Kubernetes, and high-scale, multi-region distributed systems. Advocated for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Container Instances (ACI), and Azure Front Door, collaborating with those product teams and the Helm team.
•   Spoke on Kubernetes, AKS, container internals, and distributed systems at Microsoft Ignite The Tour (7 cities, 3 continents), GOTO Chicago, Config Management Camp, and Microsoft Tech Summit.
•   Co-taught a two-day Kubernetes workshop at O'Reilly Velocity 2018.
•   Live-streamed Rust and Go development on Twitch, including rtmp-switcher and embedded programming with the Rust Discovery book.
•   Partnered with NVIDIA and a coworker to build an AI-based object detection home security system on stream, running NVIDIA DeepStream on Jetson embedded hardware with Azure IoT Edge. The project ended with a podcast-style interview with NVIDIA's embedded team.

positions.description: Gopher Academy organizes an annual US based conference for the Go programming language.

positions.title: Chief Technology Officer
positions.description:
•   Led engineering for a licensed AI voice platform that trained and served voice models of major-label artists.
•   Designed and built the platform's training infrastructure, including GPU machines for training and inference running containerized workloads with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit.
•   Designed the platform's Go services and Terraform-managed cloud infrastructure and built them with the engineering team.
•   Partnered with the AI team on custom PyTorch model development.
•   Hooky produced Lauv's "Love U Like That (Korean Version)," the first song by a major Western artist translated with AI.

positions.title: Systems Architect III
positions.description:
•   Designed and built a linear video streaming and multiplexing platform on Linux, Docker, and Kubernetes, with in-house components in Go. It replaced specialized hardware and delivered live cable channels to millions of customers nationwide.
•   Wrote a network-aware Kubernetes scheduler for blade server clusters that placed workloads using live SNMP traffic data to avoid saturating chassis and top-of-rack switch links.
•   Wrote a CNI plugin for software-defined networking within the blade servers and built custom Kubernetes operators.
•   Contributed patches to Docker and Kubernetes, including real-time thread support in Docker.
•   Integrated hardware security modules (HSMs) and secure enclaves into the multiplexing and streaming systems, working with the teams that built the video encryption ASICs.
•   Presented the platform in the closing keynote at KubeCon 2016 (~1,500 attendees).

projects.title: SkyDNS
projects.description:
SkyDNS is a distributed service for announcement and discovery of services. It leverages Raft for high-availability and consensus, and utilizes DNS queries to discover available services. This is done by leveraging SRV records in DNS, with special meaning given to subdomains, priorities and weights.

SkyDNS will also act as a forwarding DNS proxy, so that you can set your SkyDNS instance as the primary DNS service in /etc/resolv.conf and SkyDNS will forward and proxy requests for which it is not authoritative.
